dossier.public_summary: The dip alternates between deep and shallow events two-and-a-half times deeper at odd epochs, and its depth changes more than twofold between TESS sectors and even between transits in the same pipeline. That pattern fits a blended eclipsing binary at half the reported period, not a steady planet transit on the target M dwarf, with no credible on-target centroid to rule it out.

reasons.why: Odd and even transits differ by >5 sigma with a 2.5x depth ratio, strong evidence for an eclipsing binary at twice the period (29.4 d) rather than a repeating planet.
Depth changes by more than a factor of two between sectors (8567 ppm in sector 86 vs 2900 ppm in sector 59) with p_constant 5.776e-7, inconsistent with a stable planetary transit.

Depth variation is real, not a calibration offset: QLP p_constant 8.70561751194303e-08 between 2900±526 ppm and 8567±919 ppm, while SPOC at 4558±723 ppm. Simultaneous odd-even and sector changes match a blended EB with sector-dependent dilution.
Individual transits are inconsistent (chi2 52.08 dof 3): epoch 0 BTJD 2916.36 depth_ppm 196 sigma -5.4 and epoch 49 BTJD 3637.282 depth_ppm 8567 sigma 4.6 bound the signal, not a few consistent dips.

Machine-learned planet score 0.07 is in the lowest decile for former planets, consistent with binary/blend false positives; secondary snr 4.397 at phase 0.2212 and fit_b 0.944 grazing morphology further support EB.
